hints.title: Choose the correct branch each time
hints.body: The rule depends on whether the product is a multiple of 3. For a multiple, choose a factorisation that connects it to the function value being asked for.
hints.recap: A piecewise definition must be applied using the condition on its input.
hints.pitfall: The condition concerns the product, not whether both factors are multiples of three.
hints.pause: Write useful factorisations for the three inputs in the given equation.

recall.reminder: A piecewise definition must be applied using the condition on its input.

hints.title: Use one unknown function value
hints.body: Let t=f(3). Use the definition to express the three terms of the given equation in terms of t or known integers. Then substitute them into that equation.
hints.recap: Renaming a repeated function value can turn a functional relation into an ordinary equation.
hints.pitfall: A non-multiple of three uses the direct-value branch; do not leave such values as new unknowns.
hints.pause: Form and solve the equation in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow></math>, then identify which option it gives.

recall.reminder: Renaming a repeated function value can turn a functional relation into an ordinary equation.

solution:
1. Apply the two branches. Since 9=3×3 is a multiple of 3, f(9)=f(3)2. The input 16 is not a multiple of 3, so f(16)=16. Also 24=3×8, giving f(24)=f(3)f(8)=8f(3) because f(8)=8.

2. Rename the unknown. Put t=f(3). The given condition becomes t2+16−8t=0, or (t−4)2=0. Thus f(3)=4.

3. Check. With this value, f(9)=16 and f(24)=32, so the original condition is 16+16−32=0.

Answer F.
knowledgePattern: Apply a piecewise multiplicative function rule and solve the resulting quadratic in a function value
